sources.citation: Carrington, Lois. 1996. A linguistic bibliography of the New Guinea area. Pacific Linguistics D-90 (language index entries Binahari, Ma, Neme, Neme'a, Nemea).
sources.note: Bibliographic only: Binahari = Voegelins 1965, Wurm & Hattori 1981; Ma = Thomson 1975, 1975; Neme'a = Strong 1919 ('Vocabularies - Neme'a tribe', Papua Ann. Rep. 1917-18: 110), Thomson 1975, 1975. No descriptive work listed.

sources.citation: Dutton, T. E. 1975. South-Eastern Trans-New Guinea Phylum languages. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 1: Papuan languages and the New Guinea linguistic scene, 613-664. Pacific Linguistics C-38. doi:10.15144/PL-C38.613
sources.note: Sec. 2.9.5.5 (p. 638): 'None of the languages except Magi (or Mailu) has been studied or recorded in any detail.' Sec. 2.9.5.5.4 Binahari (pp. 639-640) repeats the 1971 geography and notes Thomson's view that Neme and Ma are separate languages. Only a stock-wide generality on p. 622 ('Some languages are tonal but stress is generally important and related to intonation'), not about Binahari.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid records bina1274 (Binahari-Ma) and bina1275 (Binahari-Neme), JSON endpoints.
sources.note: Bibliographic only. bina1274 has zero references; Ethnologue comment says Binahari-Ma 'is arguably a distinct language from Binahari-Neme' (citing Dutton, hh:hv:Dutton:Mailu:93). bina1275 refs: Dutton 1975 (overview), Ray 1938 (overview), Dutton 1999 (overview), Bastard 1920 (wordlist). No grammar, sketch or phonology exists in Glottolog's record for either.

sources.citation: Greenhill, S. J. (ed.). TransNewGuinea.org, language page 'Binahari' (bina1275 / bxz), 102 lexical items from source 'Summer Institute of Linguistics Language Survey of Binahari, 1985'.
sources.note: Phonetic wordlist (e.g. ɛmɛkʰ 'man', guʔu 'belly', haᵘřa 'two'); no stress or accent marks; the page does not say whether the 1985 SIL survey list is Ma or Neme'a (the forms emek 'man', gap 'shoulder' match Thomson's MN = Neme'a column, so probably Neme'a).

sources.citation: Dutton, T. E. 1982. Borrowing in Austronesian and non-Austronesian languages of coastal south-east mainland Papua New Guinea. In A. Halim, L. Carrington & S. A. Wurm (eds), Papers from the Third International Conference on Austronesian Linguistics, vol. 1: Currents in Oceanic, 109-177. Pacific Linguistics C-74. doi:10.15144/PL-C74.109
sources.note: Treats Ma (c. 600 speakers) and Neme'a (c. 200) as separate Mailuan languages (p. 111 and note 1). Chart 1 (p. 115) gives a synchronic segment inventory for Ma (p/f, t/s, k not medially, b, d, g, h, m, n, l/r, v/w, y; i e a o u) and Chart 2 (pp. 115-116) proto-Mailuan reflexes (PMF *t > Ma s, *r > r, *k > k); Appendix 2 sound laws. Data are unphonemicised wordlist forms; nothing on stress, accent or prosody anywhere in the paper (grep: 0).

sources.citation: Thomson, N. P. 1975. Magi phonology and grammar -- fifty years afterwards. In T. E. Dutton (ed.), Studies in languages of central and south-east Papua, 599-666. Pacific Linguistics C-29. doi:10.15144/PL-C29.599
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: not located online or at Harvard
sources.note: Describes Magi (Mailu, mail1248) only: sec. 2.5 (pp. 605-606) stress usually penultimate, sometimes antepenultimate, never final. Does not mention Binahari, Ma or Neme'a (grep: 0). Nearest-relative comparison only; NOT a statement about Ma.

sources.citation: Thomson, N. P. 1975. The dialects of Magi. In R. Conrad, W. Dye, N. P. Thomson & L. Bruce (eds), Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 18, 37-90. Pacific Linguistics A-40. doi:10.15144/PL-A40.37
sources.note: Sec. 2.12.3 'Binahari' (pp. 47-48): Ma (Darava No. 2 list) and Neme'a (Bam list) share only 60% basic vocabulary, so 'Binahari now becomes a blanket term to cover these two separate languages of the Mailuan Family'. Comparative wordlists (abbrev. MMa = Mada'a, MN = Neme'a) carry no stress marks; no statement on stress or accent.

sources.citation: Dutton, T. E. 1971. Languages of south-east Papua: a preliminary report. In T. E. Dutton, C. L. Voorhoeve & S. A. Wurm, Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 14, 1-46. Pacific Linguistics A-28. Canberra: ANU. doi:10.15144/PL-A28.1 (whole volume, ANU hdl 1885/145019)
sources.note: Sec. 4.44 'Binahari' (pp. 24-25): geography, two dialects Neme (from nemeda'a) and Ma (from mada'a), Ma spoken by 172 people in Oi'o and Darava No. 2; lexicostatistics and village lists only. No phonology and nothing on stress or accent (spacing-tolerant grep of the Dutton paper: 0 hits; the only stress remarks in the volume are in Voorhoeve's and Wurm's papers on other languages).

sources.citation: ASJP (lexibank-asjp) lists BINAHARI (Ray 1938), BINAHARI_MA (Grist 1926, Papua Annual Report 1925-26: 95, 'Name of Tribe Bina-hari, Name of Village Darava') and BINAHARI_NEMEA (Bastard 1920).
sources.note: Source records only; identifies Grist 1926 (Darava village) as the one early wordlist specifically of Ma. No stress information.
